Review this single coherent mathematical theorem package rigorously. Return ACCEPT or REVISE and explain substantive errors, missing hypotheses, missed source roles, or double counting. Do not certify execution of Python or Lean. The preceding accepted internal-chain theorem is included first, followed by the new renewed-support escape note. Focus on whether the new ordinary general proofs cover all stated parameters, on the positive tail charge phase and exact 2 new full tiles / 9 new events, and on the interior escape exclusion. Distinguish a partial endpoint-disjoint inventory obstruction from a complete-model counterexample. All inequalities use full ORIGINAL source data, never reconstructed supports after consumption.

Canonical U(H,d,f): H even>=6, d,f even>=4. Endpoints are rows0,1 columns1..H, plus (r,1) for2<=r<=d and(r,H) for2<=r<=f. Matching: row0 edges(1,2),(3,4),...,(H-1,H); row1 edges(2,3),(4,5),...,(H-2,H-1); both leg columns1,H pair rows(1,2),(3,4),... to their terminal. ORIGINAL supports are(0,0),(0,H+1),(d+1,1),(f+1,H), plus (r,0 if r even else2) on2..d, and(r,H+1 if r even elseH-1) on2..f. A source charge is |matching|+|original supports in endpoint tiles|-2|endpoint tiles|. Physical tiles are rows{2r,2r+1} times columns{2c,2c+1}. F counts full tiles not wholly in a single original. Directed events are(owner,endpoint,target) with adjacent endpoints of different originals in the same physical tile and target not in the source owner's original-support set. Phi=N+sum negative charge magnitudes+2|F|-|events|. A complete feasible family has pairwise-disjoint original endpoint sets; all unconsumed original supports in their UNION occupied set have degree exactly1, all endpoints have occupied degree>=3. The arguments use completeness only as a necessary condition to force absent supports into another actual original.

Standard rotor endpoints: (1,2),(2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,3),(4,3),(3,2),(3,1). Original supports: (0,2),(1,1),(2,5),(1,4),(5,3),(4,4),(3,0),(4,1). Matching: (2,2)-(1,2), (2,3)-(2,4), (3,3)-(4,3), (3,2)-(3,1).

Review the ENTIRE new note, including Section5 specified-owner compensation and its still-incomplete scope. This is a fresh full self-contained review after the previous worker failed during typing, not a request to certify that failed task.

# Internal-consumer chains, fresh forced owners and zero-gain repairs

21 October 2026. This addresses the selected-consumer-outside-bases hypothesis
in the [packed batch theorem](SECONDARY_TEN_BATCH_TERMINAL_BUDGET.md).
There are arbitrarily long endpoint-disjoint dependency paths, with zero
signed contact remainder, for which the sum of the local baselines fails.
Completeness forces one fresh negative U per block, with no owner reuse.
Nevertheless a simultaneous family of fresh consumers has exactly zero
net gain because of occupied adjacent bands. These are partial-inventory
obstructions to proposed rules, not counterexamples to the complete-model
inequality or the global5/6 target.

## 1. The full-original chain

Fix n>=1. Choose independent even w_i>=12 and z_i>=24, an odd a_0,
an even s_0, and an even h>=6. For i=0,...,n-2 set

    a_(i+1)=a_i+z_i-6,     s_(i+1)=s_i-w_(i+1)-12.

Let A_i be the second prescribed eight-original residual with parameters
a_i,w_i,k_i=w_i+10,z_i, translated by (0,s_i). All transformations act
on the ORIGINAL matching, support and endpoint sets. In particular

    V_i=U(w_i+10,8,z_i),
    (r,c)->(a_i-6+r,w_i+12+s_i-c).

For clarity the complete A_i charts are below; add s_i to every column
in the last column. These are the existing residual originals, not new
replacement copies with reconstructed support data.

| Owner | Canonical dimensions | Chart at a=a_i,w=w_i, before column shift |
|---|---|---|
| Q | U(6,8,4) | (a+11-c,11-r) |
| D | U(w+4,10,4) | (a-2+r,5+c) |
| L | U(w,4,6) | (a+r,6+c) |
| C | U(8,6,4) | (a+6-r,w+6+c) |
| E | U(6,4,4) | (a+4-r,w+7+c) |
| W | U(6,4,4) | (a+1+c,w+1+r) |
| T0 | U(w+6,6,4) | (a-4+r,w+11-c) |
| V | U(w+10,8,z) | (a-6+r,w+12-c) |

Adjoin the north east-terminal rotor R_i=R_N at
t_i=(a_i+1,x_i), where x_i=w_i+14+s_i, and put B_i=A_i+R_i.
The unconsumed upper support is e_i=(a_i,x_i). Define the single root

    K=U(h,6,4), (r,c)->(a_0-6+r,w_0+13+s_0+c),
    H_0=(union_i B_i) union {K},     b_i=w_i+9.

**Chain obstruction theorem.** All9n+1 original endpoint sets in H_0
are pairwise disjoint, the B_i are disjoint actual-owner sets, and

    Phi(H_0)=sum_i b_i+h-1-n.                         (1)

The n new mixed full tiles outside the internal B_i are precisely

    T_i={a_i-1,a_i} x {x_i,x_i+1}.

Each has exactly the two directed events between (a_i,x_i) and
(a_i,x_i+1), one in each direction. Thus their total signed contribution
is zero and there is no further exterior event or full-tile remainder.

The actual upper U for B_0 is K. For i>=1 it is the already counted
owner V_(i-1). Indeed leg exchange rewrites that FULL original as

    U(w_(i-1)+10,z_(i-1),8),
    (r,c)->(a_i-z_(i-1)+r,w_i+13+s_i+c).

The recurrence gives both coordinate equalities. Even breadth and leg
lengths make leg exchange preserve the matching and ORIGINAL supports.
The resulting dependencies B_i->B_(i-1)->...->B_0->K form a path.

In particular n>h-1 gives Phi(H_0)<sum_i b_i, despite acyclicity and
zero signed exterior remainder. The deficit can be arbitrarily large
with the root fixed. Absolute Phi(H_0)=sum_i(w_i+8)+h-1 is positive.
This does not refute any complete-model target.

### General geometric proof

Separate the long far stem of V_i from the body of B_i. Every remaining
endpoint lies between rows a_i-6 and a_i+10. Every B_i endpoint has
column at least s_i+2. Its largest column is x_i+3, on its rotor.
The body of B_(i+1) starts at row a_i+z_i-12>=a_i+12, leaving no
shared endpoint tile or adjacency with the preceding body. V_i's near
stem and bar lie to the right or above that later body. Its far stem is
exactly the upper-right U in the later block's chart. The accepted
upper-right/north-rotor receipt gives only T_(i+1) and its two events.

For j>=i+2, the maximum B_j column is at most s_i-19, whereas every
B_i endpoint has column at least s_i+2. Thus nonadjacent bases have no
shared endpoint tile or adjacency. The root K is disjoint from B_0
by the upper-right receipt; it lies at columns at least x_0 and has no
contact with later blocks, whose largest column is at most s_0+5.
These facts prove endpoint disjointness and exhaust all cross contacts.

Each base has Phi(B_i)=b_i-1 by the accepted residual and north-rotor
receipts. K contributes h-1 once. Its contact with R_0 is neutral.
Adding the n neutral cross tiles proves(1). No mass for V_(i-1) can
be added a second time when it is selected by B_i: that actual original
already belongs to B_(i-1). This is the precise failure of extending the
packed formula without its outside-bases hypothesis.

## 2. Completeness forces n distinct fresh negative owners

For each block put

    p_i=(a_i+2,w_i+12+s_i)=(a_i+2,x_i-2).

**Fresh-owner lemma.** If a complete feasible original U/rotor family G
contains H_0, the actual owners P_i of the p_i are n distinct U originals
outside H_0. Every P_i has charge1-H_i, with even H_i>=6. Consequently
their negative mass, counted once per actual owner, is

    M=sum_i(H_i-1)>=5n.                             (2)

**Proof.** The point p_i is V_i's ORIGINAL support(8,0). It is absent
from B_i and its rotor. Every preceding block has minimum endpoint column
s_j+2=x_(j+1)>=x_i, while p_i has column x_i-2. Every later block
starts at row at least a_i+12. The root has columns at least x_0>=x_i.
Hence p_i is absent from H_0. The preceding body row maximum is only
bounded by a_i-8 when z_(i-1)=24; no stronger row separation is used.
Its three foreign endpoint neighbors are

    west:  V_i:(a_i+2,x_i-3),
    east:  E_i:(a_i+2,x_i-1),
    south: E_i:(a_i+3,x_i-2).

An unconsumed original support would have at least three occupied
neighbors, contradicting completeness. Its actual consumer must have
its own matching partner north, its only available own-neighbor direction.
The two north-tip rotors both contain E_i:(a_i,x_i-1), so neither can
be its owner. This is the same full-rotor collision used in the accepted
[depth-eight proof](SECONDARY_TEN_DEPTH_EIGHT_COMPLETE_EXCLUSION.md).
Thus it is a north-terminal U, in one of the two frames

    (r,c)->(a_i+2-d+r,w_i+11+s_i+c),
    (r,c)->(a_i+2-d+r,w_i+13+s_i-c),

with arbitrary even breadth H_i>=6 and depths d,f>=4. These frames are
even translations of the accepted upper-U frames, so q(P_i)=1-H_i.

All p_i have odd row and even column. The two leg terminals of ANY
legal U have opposite checkerboard colors: in intrinsic coordinates
their coordinate sums differ by f-d+H_i-1, an odd integer. This property
survives every integer grid isometry. Since p_i are distinct points of
the same checkerboard color, two of them cannot be terminals of the
same original. Thus all P_i are distinct and outside H_0. This proves(2),
with no copied source mass or reused terminal. In particular the weak
two-terminal capacity estimate is unnecessary here.

For their actual union P, persistence and exact set differences give

    Phi(H_0 union P)=sum_i b_i+h-1-n+M+2|F_new|-|E_new|. (3)

Here the new sets are differences against the full H_0 inventory and
include every P/base and P/P interaction. Therefore

    Phi(H_0 union P)>=sum_i b_i+h-1+4n+2|F_new|-|E_new|.

This is a source-mass and exact-ledger result. A favorable sign for the
new contact term is not assumed, and(2) alone is not a compensation theorem.

## 3. All n fresh consumers can have zero gain simultaneously

There is a general choice of the forced owners at p_i that is endpoint
disjoint from the entire H_0 and from every other such choice:

    P_i^0=U(w_i+12,10,4),
    (r,c)->(a_i-8+r,w_i+13+s_i-c),
    H_1=H_0 union {P_i^0:0<=i<n}.

Each P_i^0 consumes p_i and is a different actual full original. Yet

    Phi(H_1)=Phi(H_0)=sum_i b_i+h-1-n.              (4)

Here is the exact full-tile and event computation. Its original charge
is -(w_i+11). Its bar endpoint row a_i-7 is adjacent to V_i's bar
row a_i-6. Over the k_i=w_i+10 columns s_i+2 through s_i+w_i+11,
there are k_i/2 aligned full tiles, each with FOUR surviving directed
events. Neither direction targets an original support; the V target
has intrinsic row-1 and the P target row2 in a non-stem column. The V endpoints in
that band have no original support to the north, and the P bar endpoints
have no original support to the south in those columns. The band
therefore contributes signed value-k_i.

The remaining contact is with E_i in the near-stem column. It consists
of one three-endpoint tile at rows a_i-1,a_i and one full2+2 tile at
rows a_i+1,a_i+2, both in columns x_i-2,x_i-1. Its three events are

    E_i:(a_i,x_i-1)       -> P_i^0:(a_i,x_i-2),
    E_i:(a_i+2,x_i-1)     -> P_i^0:(a_i+2,x_i-2),
    P_i^0:(a_i+1,x_i-2)   -> E_i:(a_i+1,x_i-1).

Thus this contact has (DeltaF,DeltaE)=(1,3), signed value-1.
The total increment is exactly

    (w_i+11)+2*(k_i/2+1)-(2*k_i+3)=0.

These contacts cannot overlap different i. P_i^0 ends at row a_i+2;
P_(i+1)^0 starts at row a_i+z_i-14>=a_i+10. Every preceding B_j has
minimum endpoint column at least x_i, while P_i^0 has maximum endpoint
column x_i-2. Thus its entire preceding inventory is separated by at
least two columns, even when the endpoint row ranges meet. Later blocks
start at row at least a_i+12. P_i^0's far stem is in
column s_i+1, immediately left of V_i's column s_i+2, but those two
columns belong to different tiles; its only band contact is the one
already counted. The root is also two columns beyond P_0^0's near
stem, in a different tile column. This proves the disjointness and
exhaustiveness needed to sum the increments and proves(4).

**Explicit remaining incompleteness.** For every i,

    q_i=(a_i-3,s_i+1)

is P_i^0's original far axial support and is absent from H_1. It sees
the retained P_i^0 far terminal(a_i-4,s_i+1) to the north and V_i's
far-stem endpoint(a_i-3,s_i+2) to the east. Thus it must be consumed
in any complete extension. This proves H_1 is incomplete even though
all the p_i have been consumed. No nonextendibility is claimed.

## 4. Consequences and verification scope

The path family disproves the endpoint-only rules that acyclic internal
borrowing is safe, or that fresh negative consumers automatically provide
positive net repair. Both failures have exact general receipts. They do
not disprove the complete-model inequality: H_0 and H_1 are incomplete,
their absolute Phi is positive, and subsequent forced consumers may repair
the relative deficit. The outside-bases hypothesis of the accepted packed
theorem remains necessary for its stated formula.

The fresh-owner lemma also gives constructive positive information:
completeness forces n unused original-owner budgets, all distinct by
checkerboard color. The occupied-band computation explains exactly why
their charge cannot be used without debiting their contacts in the same
ledger. The next question is the actual q_i-consumer closure and its
joint signed remainder, not a new count of the already exhausted P_i^0
mass. The global5/6 improvement and rectangular-grid triple equality remain
open; the submitted11October manuscript is unchanged.

The general proofs above do not use an enumeration cutoff. The companion
checker reconstructs full ORIGINAL sources and verifies exact physical
full-tile and owner-labelled event SETS, including nonuniform chains.
The standalone Lean file verifies local coordinate, parity, budget and
renewed-support certificates. Complete ownership/role classification,
the general inter-block separation and final set partition remain ordinary
proofs; local formalization is not an end-to-end certificate.

Validation:96 exact chain/zero-gain set controls, three nonuniform chains
of7,12,24 blocks, eight tile-preserving isometries,288 full-original
terminal parity controls and24 full-original rotor exclusions PASS.
The8-block witness has baseline168 and Phi165, both before and after
the eight zero-gain consumers; the latter add mass184,96 full tiles and
376 directed events, giving184+192-376=0. It remains incomplete at
eight explicitly listed renewed supports.

All34 declarations, including24 theorems, in
[the standalone Lean source](../formal/SubQuorum/SecondaryTenInternalConsumerChains.lean)
pass locally with every individual axiom list checked, no warnings and
no sorry/native axioms. The [control receipt](../output/secondary-ten-internal-consumer-controls.json)
and [Lean receipt](../output/secondary-ten-internal-consumer-lean-validation.json)
record their precise scope. A separate written-proof review is ACCEPT,
with the preceding-block column-separation justification now explicit.
Focused controls check371 preceding-block/repair column pairs and12
cases where the preceding body reaches the repair's first bar row.
It does not stand in for either execution check; see the
[review receipt](../output/secondary-ten-internal-consumer-review.json).


NEW NOTE TO REVIEW

# Renewed-support closure and the long positive tail escape

21 October 2026. This continues the [internal-consumer chain theorem](SECONDARY_TEN_INTERNAL_CONSUMER_CHAINS.md).
All originals retain their full matching, endpoint and original-support sets.
The functional is Phi=N+S+2F-E, with N the number of positive originals,
S their total negative mass, F the mixed full physical tiles and E the
owner-labelled intratile directed foreign events excluding original supports.
No charge or event resource is copied when a support is consumed.

## 1. Setting and statements

Use all hypotheses, coordinates and original owners of that theorem:
n>=1, independent even w_i>=12 and z_i>=24, odd a_0, even s_0,
even root breadth h>=6, and

    a_(i+1)=a_i+z_i-6,   s_(i+1)=s_i-w_(i+1)-12.

Its H1 contains the9n+1 base/root originals and the n zero-gain repairs
P_i^0=U(w_i+12,10,4), chart(a_i-8+r,w_i+13+s_i-c). Put

    q_i=(a_i-3,s_i+1),   r_i=(a_i-2,s_i+1).

Let R be the standard eight-endpoint rotor of the source catalogue. Adjoin
the following FULL originals, not just their local endpoints:

    Z_i=R,            chart(a_i-5+r,s_i-3+c),
    L_i=U(6,4,4),     chart(a_i+2-r,s_i+2-c),
    H2=H1 union {Z_i:0<=i<n},
    H3=H2 union {L_i:0<=i<n}.

**Zero-gain closure theorem.** These originals are pairwise endpoint-disjoint.
Every Z_i consumes q_i and has charge0, no new mixed full tile and no new
directed event. Every L_i consumes r_i, has charge-1 and adds exactly one
mixed full tile and three directed events. The increments hold simultaneously:

    Phi(H3)=Phi(H2)=Phi(H1)=sum_i(w_i+9)+h-1-n.       (1)

H2 has11n+1 originals and H3 has12n+1 originals. For every i, both H2 and
H3 are incomplete at the retained original support

    t_i=(a_i-4,s_i).

**Actual-consumer alternatives.** In any complete feasible original U/rotor
family containing H2, the actual owner of r_i is a fresh south-terminal U.
Writing its breadth H and its incident/other depths d,f, all even with
H>=6 and d,f>=4, leg exchange gives exactly two possible endpoint/support/
matching frames:

    left:  U(H,d,f), chart(a_i+d-2-r,s_i+2-c), charge-1;
    right: U(H,d,f), chart(a_i+d-2-r,s_i+c),   charge+1.     (2)

The right frame requires d>=z_i-2. If i<n-1, that same frame collides
with E_(i+1), so every interior r_i must have a left-frame owner.
All n actual owners are distinct: the r_i have the same checkerboard color
and the two terminals of one legal U have opposite colors. Consequently
at least n-1 distinct fresh charge-1 originals are forced by H2. This is
an ownership statement, not a net-compensation estimate for arbitrary owners.

**Long positive tail obstruction.** Put a=a_(n-1), s=s_(n-1), w=w_(n-1),
z=z_(n-1). For ANY even d>=z-2, the FULL original

    J=U(w,d,d-6), chart(a+d-2-r,s+c)                    (3)

is endpoint-disjoint from H2 and from all L_i with i<n-1. It consumes the
last r, has charge+1, and its EXACT increment relative to their union is

    DeltaN=1, DeltaS=0, DeltaF=2, DeltaE=9, DeltaPhi=-4. (4)

Thus the union with J in place of the last L has

    Phi=sum_i(w_i+9)+h-1-n-4.                         (5)

It is still incomplete at every t_i. This refutes the proposed endpoint-only
rule that a renewed-support consumer necessarily has nonnegative marginal
Phi. It neither refutes a rule with complete-extension hypotheses nor the
complete-model inequality or global5/6 target. Extendibility is not asserted.

## 2. Proof of simultaneous closure and retained incompleteness

Relative to (a_i,s_i), the endpoints of Z_i are

    (-4,-1),(-3,-1),(-3,0),(-3,1),
    (-2,-2),(-2,-1),(-2,0),(-1,0).

Its original supports are

    (-5,-1),(-4,-2),(-4,1),(-3,2),
    (-2,-3),(-1,-2),(-1,1),(0,0).

The single-source charge is0 by its four original matching edges and
its original-support/tile count. The endpoints do not meet H1: its eastern
tip q lies just below the P^0 far terminal; all other Z endpoints have
columns at most s_i. Its only possible old endpoint adjacencies are with
that P^0 terminal and with V_i's column s_i+2. The first crosses a physical
tile-row boundary; the second crosses a tile-column boundary. There is no
new intratile adjacency and no new mixed full tile. In particular no new
directed event is being discarded merely because its target became occupied.

The endpoints of L_i have near stem column s_i+1 and far stem column
s_i-4, between rows a_i-2 and a_i+2, and the two bar rows a_i+1,a_i+2.
The stems stop above at row a_i-2. They avoid Z and H1. The only new
mixed full tile is

    {a_i-3,a_i-2} x {s_i,s_i+1}.

Its three old cells are in Z_i, and its fourth is r_i in L_i. The exact
three new directed events are

    Z_i:(a_i-3,s_i+1) -> L_i:(a_i-2,s_i+1),
    Z_i:(a_i-2,s_i)   -> L_i:(a_i-2,s_i+1),
    L_i:(a_i-2,s_i+1) -> Z_i:(a_i-2,s_i).

The reverse event from r_i to q_i is excluded because q_i is L_i's
original axial support. At (a_i-1,s_i+1), the west Z endpoint is an
original L support, so it supplies no extra event. The far L stem has
column s_i-4, at least two columns left of every Z endpoint. Contacts
with V_i's column s_i+2 cross tile columns. Thus the lists are exhaustive.
The phase of L gives charge-1; its increment is1+2-3=0.

These local partitions persist in the full chain. All preceding B_j
have minimum column at least x_i=s_i+w_i+14. Preceding P_j^0 have
minimum column at least s_i+w_i+13. They are separated from Z_i and L_i
by columns. The root lies still farther right. For j>i, the body of B_j
starts at row at least a_i+12; its long stem starts no earlier than that
body's lower row bound. The new endpoints have maximum row a_i+2.
For new originals at adjacent indices, their row ranges are separated
by at least12: a_(i+1)-4>=a_i+14, whereas the current maximum is a_i+2.
No additional full tile or event is possible. This proves(1).

The point t_i is P_i^0's original far side support with intrinsic
coordinates(4,w_i+13). It is absent from both enlarged endpoint sets.
Its retained endpoint neighbors are

    west Z_i:(a_i-4,s_i-1),
    east P_i^0:(a_i-4,s_i+1),
    south Z_i:(a_i-3,s_i).

An unconsumed support with these three occupied neighbors contradicts
the required degree1. This proves incompleteness without counting other
unresolved support obligations.

## 3. Proof of the actual-owner alternatives

The absent r_i is V_i's original side support with intrinsic(4,w_i+11).
In H2 it has the three foreign endpoint neighbors

    north Z_i:q_i, west Z_i:(a_i-2,s_i),
    east V_i:(a_i-2,s_i+2).

Completeness therefore forces r_i to be consumed. The consuming original
can only have its own matching neighbor south. A U endpoint with exactly
one own endpoint neighbor is a leg terminal. Exchanging the full original
legs gives the two frames(2), with no depth restriction imported from an
enumeration. There are two full south-tip rotor possibilities. The first
contains V_i:(a_i-1,s_i+2), and the second contains Z_i:(a_i-1,s_i).
Both are excluded by endpoint disjointness. This exhausts the catalogue.

For clarity, the charge phases in(2) can be counted directly. Set
H=2b,d=2u,f=2v and R=a_i+d-2, which is odd. Both frames have
2b-1+u+v matching edges. For the right frame the endpoint-tile count is
b+1+u+v and the original-support-inside count is u+v+4, giving charge+1.
For the left frame those counts are b+u+v and u+v, giving charge-1.
Every count uses original supports, including ones subsequently consumed.

For the right frame, a bar endpoint lies in column s_i+2 at row
R-1=a_i+d-3. If d<z_i-2, evenness gives d<=z_i-4. This row is then
between a_i-4 and a_i+z_i-6, on V_i's retained far stem: a collision.
Thus d>=z_i-2. If i<n-1, the right frame's near stem, including its
top bar cell, covers column s_i+1 from row a_i-2 through
R>=a_i+z_i-4. The next block has

    E_(i+1):(a_(i+1),w_(i+1)+13+s_(i+1))
           =(a_i+z_i-6,s_i+1).

That retained endpoint belongs to the near stem, a contradiction. Right
escape is therefore a genuine tail alternative only. It is not missing
from the catalogue simply because short-depth controls cannot reach it.

All r_i have odd row and odd column, hence the same checkerboard color.
The full-original terminal-color lemma of the chain theorem proves their
owners distinct. They are outside H2 because every r_i is absent there.
This proves the stated fresh-owner consequence.

## 4. Exact tail debit and separation proof

For J in(3), the near stem has column s+1, starting at row a-2, and the
far stem has column s+w, starting at row a+4. Its bar rows are
R-1,R with R=a+d-2>=a+z-4. They lie below every local body, whose
last row is at most a+10. At the smallest d, the lower V terminal is
at row a+z-6, odd, while the upper J bar row a+z-5 is even: they lie
in different tile rows. For larger d they are farther separated.

The near stem avoids P^0, whose far terminal is at a-4; its other
old endpoints in the same tile column belong to Z. The far stem starts
below the Q/D/L/T0/V bars; Q has columns at most s+11<s+w. All C/E
stems have columns greater than s+w. W has its left bar column at

## 5. A simultaneous specified-owner compensation lemma

This section was added after submission of the initial review request; its
review scope must be tracked separately.

There is a full-original choice for all t_i-consumers that compensates the
original chain deficit, even with the negative tail. Set

    Y_i=U(w_i+14,6,4), chart(a_i-10+r,s_i-1+c).

**Specified-owner compensation lemma.** All Y_i are endpoint-disjoint from
one another and from H3. Each consumes t_i, has charge-(w_i+13), and its
increment relative to the whole simultaneous union is

    DeltaS=w_i+13, DeltaF=w_i/2+10,
    DeltaE=2*w_i+32, DeltaPhi=1.                     (6)

Consequently the exact two joint ledgers are

    Phi(H3 union all Y_i)=sum_i(w_i+9)+h-1,
    Phi(H2 union {L_i:i<n-1} union {J} union all Y_i)
                         =sum_i(w_i+9)+h-5.         (7)

The second has at least one unit beyond the sum of baselines because h>=6.
This is a conditional local compensation lemma when the specified Y_i
actually occur in the inventory. No existence or completeness assertion is
needed to calculate these full-original unions. It gives no monotonicity
claim for arbitrary further originals.

**Proof.** Work relative to (a_i,s_i), writing w=w_i. The Y bar occupies
rows-10,-9 and columns0..w+13. Its near stem is in column0 through row-4;
its far stem is in column w+13 through row-6. The only foreign original
with an intratile contact is P_i^0, whose bar occupies rows-8,-7 and
columns1..w+12, far stem is column1 through row-4 and near stem is
column w+12 through row2. The Y charge is1-(w+14)=-(w+13), by the
same north-terminal phase count as the accepted chain theorem.

The new full tiles have exactly the following lower-left coordinates in
this relative chart (tile row and column minima):

    (-9,2j),  j=0,...,(w+12)/2,
    (-7,0), (-5,0), (-7,w+12).

There are w/2+7 top-band tiles and three stem tiles. The new directed
events comprise the following disjoint lists:

    Y:(-9,c) -> P^0:(-8,c), and reverse, c=1,...,w+12;
    Y:(j,0) -> P^0:(j,1), j=-8,-6,-4;
    P^0:(j,1) -> Y:(j,0), j=-7,-5;
    Y:(j,w+13) -> P^0:(j,w+12), j=-8,-6;
    P^0:(-7,w+12) -> Y:(-7,w+13).

The first list has2(w+12) events, the others5+3. In the band the targets
have intrinsic non-stem row2 for Y, or row-1 for P^0, and are not original
supports. In the stem lists the omitted reverse directions are exactly
the original axial/bar-exterior or parity-dependent lateral supports.
These support tests use the original sets even though several supports
are already consumed. This proves the exact counts in(6).

To exhaust the exterior, local B_i endpoints have columns at least s_i+2
and rows at least a_i-6. Y's bar is above them and its near stem is to
their left. Its far stem ends at row a_i-6. The east rotor starts at
row a_i-1, and L/C/E/W start at row a_i or later, so none can reach that
stem. V and T0 have maximum
columns s_i+w_i+11 and s_i+w_i+10, respectively, to its left. D and Q
also lie to its left. Thus no local B endpoint shares an intratile edge
with Y. Z has no intratile adjacency to its tip t: Z's west neighbor
crosses a tile-column boundary and its south neighbor crosses a tile-row
boundary. L begins two rows below Y's last endpoint.

Preceding B_j have columns at least x_i=s_i+w_i+14, which is even;
Y's maximum column x_i-1 is in the preceding tile column. The root
also lies beyond that boundary. Preceding P^0/Z/L originals have maximum
row at most a_i-16, whereas Y starts at a_i-10. Subsequent originals
start below Y's last row a_i-4. Adjacent Y bar starts differ by at
least18, with a gap of at least12 between the previous Y's last endpoint
and the next Y's first endpoint. These bounds rule out any additional
event or shared full tile. They also prove all stated endpoint disjointness.

For the tail version, J starts at row a-2, two rows below the tail Y's
last endpoint; preceding Y's end still earlier. Thus J and all Y have
no intratile contact. The two tail full tiles from Section4 are also
disjoint from the Y lists. The exact increments sum, proving(7).

Both unions remain incomplete. For example the last block's retained
E original axial support u=(a-1,s+w+13), intrinsic(5,6), is still absent.
Its west P^0 endpoint(a-1,s+w+12), south E endpoint(a,s+w+13) and east
upper-consumer endpoint(a-1,s+w+14) persist. The upper consumer is the
root if n=1 and V_(n-2) otherwise. No Y or J reaches u. Thus at least
three occupied neighbors still force a later consumer; even the compensated
inventory has not been promoted to a complete-family theorem.

This identifies a genuine compensation mechanism for an entire specified
chain: a later forced owner can repay a deficit that earlier forced owners
left unchanged or worsened. It does not assert that an arbitrary actual
t_i-consumer has the receipt(6). That is the next all-parameter question.

## 6. Meaning and verification scope

This proves an arbitrary-length simultaneous closure result beyond the
previous one-stage repair. It also isolates why a depth18 catalogue was
insufficient: the right frame first clears V at d=z-2>=22, changes charge
phase, and can lose four units through the already occupied W band.
The interior-chain exclusion is a new necessary condition, not a claim
that arbitrary left consumers have zero marginal contribution. Only the
explicit L family has that conclusion.

The global question still needs a common allocation and control of all
remaining mandatory support consumers. In particular t_i supplies a
specific next obligation for both families. No finite catalogue substitutes
for the general arguments above. The submitted11October DMGT manuscript,
the primary star-forming results and the global5/6 target are unchanged.

The companion checker independently reconstructs full originals and compares
exact mixed-tile and owner-labelled event sets, including nonuniform chains,
long legs, both terminal frames and the excluded rotor roles. The standalone
Lean source certifies local blocker coordinates, unbounded collision bounds,
terminal parity and receipt arithmetic. General role completeness, charge
counts and exhaustive event partitions remain ordinary proofs, not end-to-end
Lean formalization. Execution receipts and independent review are recorded
separately after their completion.
